title: Fix non-idempotent CRD sync causing post-upgrade rollback due to Helm timestamp skew
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
A subset of Private/VPC on-prem customers experienced upgrade cycles where the operator repeatedly triggered HelmRelease rollbacks after an operator upgrade. The immediate symptom: repeated reconciliations of CRDs and HelmRelease resources that alternated between the new and old revision, causing transient workload restarts and degraded API availability (502/503) for ~30-90 minutes.

Key observations:
- Escalation ticket: CS-9124, two additional customers reported similar behaviour within the same 24h window.
- Root cause hypothesis: operator-side CRD/HelmRelease sync is non-idempotent when timestamp-based annotations from Helm/HelmRelease are preserved. During an upgrade, the operator and helm-controller race: helm-controller writes a release metadata timestamp, operator applies a CRD status patch that updates generation in a way that causes helm-controller's revision detection to think the release needs rollback. The net effect is a flip-flop reconciliation loop.
- Reproducible locally with k3d + helm v3.12 using a simulated long-running CRD post-install hook.
- Impact: 3 customers, multiple services affected, one escalated to on-call SRE and customer success.

Reproduction steps (internal):
1) Install private operator v2.7.0 and sample helm chart with CRD that sets status via a post-install hook.
2) Upgrade operator to v2.8.0 (operator image built with local patch).
3) Trigger helm-controller to apply release (helm upgrade --install) concurrently with operator reconciliation.
4) Observe alternating helm-release.revision values and controller restarts in operator logs.

Immediate mitigations implemented:
- Rolled back operator for two impacted customers where safe to the previous pinned image (operator-2.7.0) to stabilize clusters (manual rollback via customer runbook).
- Temporarily disabled operator's aggressive post-upgrade sync for newly upgraded clusters via feature flag: OP_ONPREM_SYNC_WINDOW set to 0 for affected tenants (applied via console config for Dedicated and via manifest patch for Private).
- Created temporary alert: operator.rollbacks.count > 0 for 5m -> page on-call and open incident channel.

Proposed permanent fix (design notes):
1) Make CRD/status patch logic idempotent: switch to server-side apply with managedFields-aware merge and avoid touching last-applied timestamps used by helm-controller.
2) Add explicit detection for helm-controller annotations (argocd/helmrelease.revision-like keys) and avoid updating those fields during operator reconciliation.
3) Implement optimistic reconciliation backoff for resources that show oscillating resourceVersion/revision sequences; include a circuit-breaker to avoid continuous rollbacks.
4) Provide a cluster-scoped repair job: OperatorRepairJob that can safely reconcile stuck HelmRelease objects by re-computing desired manifest and applying with a stable revision strategy.

Implementation plan and rollout:
- Phase 1 (PR + unit tests): implement server-side apply change + annotation whitelist. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/operator/pull/12345 (WIP).
- Phase 2 (canary): deploy operator-2.8.1 to internal staging and 5% of Dedicated tenants with canary routing. Monitor operator.rollbacks.count and helmcontroller.revision_flap_rate.
- Phase 3 (customer opt-in private): provide operator-2.8.1 manifest with feature flag off by default. Work with CS for a controlled upgrade window per-customer.
- Phase 4: global rollout after 48h of stable canary metrics.

Testing plan:
- Add integration test that simulates concurrent helm-controller and operator reconciliation with deterministic timing to assert no revision flip after change.
- End-to-end on k8s versions: 1.26, 1.27 in our CI infra.
- Backfill regression eval against historical customer clusters using snapshot test harness (customer-snapshots bucket).

Monitoring and rollback strategy:
- New SLI: operator.helm_revision_flap_rate (alerts if > 0.5 flips/minute for a release).
- Alert policy: critical if flips > 3 in 10m for production customer cluster -> automatic rollback to previous operator image via runbook.
- Post-deploy: 30-minute watch with on-call SRE and PM available to coordinate customer communication.

Documentation / runbooks:
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Operator+Helm+Revision+Flip+Runbook
- Customer-facing notes drafted in CS doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/CS/CS-9124

Acceptance criteria:
- PR merged and green CI.
- Canary metrics: operator.rollbacks.count = 0 and helmcontroller.revision_flap_rate < 0.01 for 48 hours across canary tenants.
- No new production escalations after staged rollout for 7 days.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Server-side apply changes require Kubernetes >=1.16 managedFields presence; clusters older than supported may behave differently. We will gate feature via a version check.
- Conservative rollout needed for Private/on-prem customers where operator upgrade path varies; requires CS coordination and manual manifests.

Next steps (owner: Jonah Kim):
- Finalize PR and add integration test (ETA 2026-03-05).
- Schedule canary deployment with SRE (ETA 2026-03-07).
- Run repair job on affected clusters to clear stuck HelmRelease objects (ETA 2026-03-09).
